story_of_day.headline: Strikes and peace talks, on the same night
story_of_day.story: The US hit Iran's Qeshm Island late Monday, the first strike there since June. Washington calls it limited and defensive, aimed at missile sites used against US assets. It came hours after Vice President Vance said a deal looked closer. Oil jumped back after dropping 6% a day earlier.
story_of_day.so_what: Both sides are running war and diplomacy at once. The midterms end today, so Trump has less reason to hold back after the vote, in either direction.
story_of_day.money_angle: Brent is about $106, down from the highs but still very elevated. It fell to $105.55 on deal hopes, then bounced on the strikes.

my_take.text: Don't chase oil in either direction right now. If you want exposure, keep it small and expect big swings after the US vote.
my_take.reasoning: Prices are trading headlines, not supply. A real deal could knock Brent well below $100 fast, while a post-election escalation could push it back up. Both outcomes are plausible, so a one-way bet is a coin flip.
my_take.wrong_if: Brent closes below $98 or above $115 within a week, which would mean one side clearly won.

cards.headline: RBA hikes for the fifth time this year
cards.story: The Reserve Bank lifted the cash rate to 4.85%, the highest since 2008. It was expected. Governor Bullock said some pain now will prevent worse pain later.
cards.so_what: Mortgage holders feel it first. High oil is feeding the inflation the RBA is fighting, so Iran news now matters to Australian rates.
cards.money_angle: AUD/USD is near 0.698; the ASX 200 is near 8,887.

cards.headline: Garment unrest tests Dhaka
cards.story: Garment workers' wage protests have run for several days and turned violent in places. Some factories have reopened. The BNP alleges an Awami League hand, while state media frames it as an attempt to create instability.
cards.so_what: Garments are Bangladesh's biggest export. Prolonged unrest risks orders going to rivals, and it turns a wage dispute into a political one.

cards.headline: A bloody end to Ukraine's longest truce
cards.story: Russian bombs killed at least 29 people at an aid centre in Komyshuvakha, with 48 missing. Overnight strikes also hit power plants and hospitals. Fighting returned to Kherson after a six-day truce, the longest of the war.
cards.so_what: The truce changed nothing on the ground. Europe is still rehearsing a peacekeeping deployment for a peace that is not close.

cards.headline: Midterm day: a vote on Trump
cards.story: Americans vote for control of both the House and Senate, currently held by Republicans. The Supreme Court refused Trump's bid to throw out about 20,000 disputed California ballots, so counting continues.
cards.so_what: A Democratic House would limit Trump at home. Foreign policy, including Iran and Ukraine, is mostly in his own hands.
cards.money_angle: S&P 500 is near 7,541, and history says markets often steady after midterms.

watch.title: Post-election Iran move
watch.text: Watch whether Washington pushes for a deal or escalates once the polls close. Brent is the quick signal.
